Subject: Tenant Hardening & Commissioning playbook — private deployment handoff

Hi Samir / Claire —

Thanks for taking time earlier this week. Attaching our recommended "Tenant Hardening & Commissioning" playbook and the updated network diagram (tenant_network_diagram_v2.pdf). This thread will be the single source for the preflight checklist and owners as we move toward the commissioning window.

High-level asks (first pass):
- Account & IAM: confirm which Medicore SAs to add to the service account allowlist; we need a list of 3 identities and intended roles by EOD Tue (owner: Claire).
- Networking: confirm VPC CIDR allocations, route table owners, and whether you will provide a NAT gateway or prefer Redwood-managed egress (owner: Samir).
- KMS & keys: confirm whether Medicore will provide a CMK or we provision a customer-managed key via your KMS. Note: rotation schedule and key access policy required for SOC evidence (owner: security@medicore.com).
- Access controls: we require MFA on all admin console accounts and a plan for emergency break-glass (owner: Claire) — see attached MFA_onboarding_instructions.docx for our suggested flows.
- Evidence pack: we will request a short evidence spreadsheet (evidence_request_medico_092026.xlsx) for audit items — please assign someone to own completing the items.

Proposed timeline:
- 9/20: Confirm account/IAM list + CIDRs
- 9/22: Finalize KMS approach and egress model
- 9/24: Kickoff commissioning window (dry-run)

If you prefer, we can convert these asks into a mutual action plan in the Redwood portal and invite your team.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internal owners once you confirm.

Best,
Irene

Thanks, Irene —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Quick notes from our side after an internal sync:
- IAM: We will provide three SAs: infra-redis (read-only), infra-deploy (full deploy), infra-monitor (metrics). Claire will send the full principal ARNs by Monday.
- Egress: Medicore prefers to manage egress (we want traffic to go through our proxy + outbound filtering). We will provide a NAT + proxy IPs; need Redwood to publish egress fingerprinting ranges for allowlist.
- KMS: Security asked for us to host the CMK in our KMS (Azure Key Vault). They want to restrict key wrap/un-wrap to a small set of service principals — I'll loop security@medicore.com for policy details.

Open questions:
1) Does Redwood require a dedicated transit subnet for the KV cache peering, or can that share the same subnet as the runtime instances?
2) For metrics exfiltration, are you able to push to our Prometheus endpoint over the VPC peer, or does Redwood require pushing into a hosted ingestion with mTLS?

We’ll attach the requested ARNs and a preliminary IP list next week.

—Samir

Samir / Claire —

Thanks for the clarifications. Short answers and owners below:
- Transit subnet: Redwood strongly prefers a dedicated transit subnet for our KV cache peering to ensure predictable MTU and to avoid accidental host-based firewall policies impacting cache traffic (owner: Ben Carter). We can work with you on CIDR sizing (we usually suggest /28 for the transit pair).
- Metrics: We can push metrics over an mTLS connection to your Prometheus push endpoint, or push into Redwood's hosted ingestion with mutual TLS (you pickup or we pickup). If you want our agents to push directly to your Prometheus, we will need your cert + endpoint and a PW rotation schedule.

Proposed internal timeline (updated):
- 9/22: Claire provides principal ARNs + egress IP list (owner: Claire Huang).
- 9/23: Medicore security sends KMS access policy (owner: security@medicore.com).
- 9/24: Dry-run kickoff; Redwood will stand up a staging tenant and run connectivity checks (owner: Marissa Cole).

Notes on hardening checklist (brief):
- Admin console access must have MFA (we'll validate via a short SSO test).
- Break-glass token: Medicore must provide an offline OIDC client (we'll store as encrypted secret in our vault).
- Audit logs: We will map our telemetry streams to your SIEM using the provided syslog endpoint (sample mapping in the attached doc).

Attached: MFA_onboarding_instructions.docx (step-by-step for your SREs). I’ll add the transit CIDR suggestion inline in the diagram on Monday.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Onboarding Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Tenant Hardening & Commissioning playbook — private deployment handoff

Hi all —

A few technical clarifications from the runtime perspective to reduce surprises during commissioning:

1) KV cache peering: dedicated transit subnet please. Our runtime establishes long-lived UDP/TCP connections with pinned MTU expectations; co-locating on the host subnet can introduce iptables rules that break persistence. Suggested: two /30s (one for each AZ pair) or a single /28 for multi-AZ.

2) NAT & egress fingerprinting: If Medicore manages NAT, please provide the full CIDR/IP ranges we should expect and any upstream TLS MITM proxies (we need cert fingerprints). If IP ranges will change during scale-up, provide the automation window so we can add them to our egress allowlist programmatically (we have a simple webhook-based allowlist sync).

3) mTLS endpoints: For Prometheus ingestion, we prefer server-auth + client certs issued by your PKI. If you prefer password-based push, we can do short-lived tokens but it increases ops friction for you.

4) KMS & key usage: If you host the CMK, ensure the key policy includes Redwood's service principal with encrypt/decrypt and generateDataKey permissions; add a path for emergency rotation. We'll provide the exact principal ARN once you confirm Azure Key Vault.

Sample security group egress rules we need (example):
- TCP 443 to your proxy IP range (owner: Medicore)
- TCP  Metrics push port (e.g., 9091) to Prometheus endpoint
- UDP/TCP on transit CIDR for KV peering (pinned ports 22000-22010)

I can drop a short reference snippet into the network diagram and the mutual action plan. Let us know if you want a 30-minute tech deep-dive before the 9/24 dry-run.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
